title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
Theorem IX restates the result of Problem V (previous page). Take the alternating series

s = ax/(αy) − ab x²/(αβ y²) + abc x³/(αβγ y³) − … .

Define the shifted tails t and u, so that s = (ax/αy)(1−t). Then

ax/s = αy/(1−t) = αy + αbxy/(bx/t − bx).

Iterating gives

ax/s = αy + αbxy/(βy − bx + βcxy/(γy − cx + γdxy/(δy − dx + …))).

In modern terms this is Euler's 'equivalent' continued fraction of a series: the n-th convergent equals the n-th partial sum. It is a special case of Euler's 1748 series-to-continued-fraction formula.

§52–55 prepare an application. Take Z(z) = ∫₀^z t^{m−1}(1+tⁿ)^{k/n−1} dt and write Z = v(1+zⁿ)^{k/n}. Differentiating and dividing by (1+zⁿ)^{k/n−1} gives the linear ODE

v′(1+zⁿ) + k zⁿ⁻¹ v − z^{m−1} = 0.

Near z = 0 we have Z ≈ z^m/m = v. So set v = A z^m − B z^{m+n} + C z^{m+2n} − … . Equating coefficients gives:
- mA = 1;
- (m+n)B = (m+k)A;
- (m+2n)C = (m+n+k)B;
- and so on.

Hence

v = z^m/m − (m+k)/(m(m+n)) z^{m+n} + (m+k)(m+n+k)/(m(m+n)(m+2n)) z^{m+2n} − … .

In modern form, Z = (z^m/m)(1+zⁿ)^{k/n} ₂F₁(1, (m+k)/n; (m+n)/n; −zⁿ). Equivalently, the Euler–Pfaff transformation of

Z = (z^m/m) ₂F₁(1−k/n, m/n; m/n+1; −zⁿ).

The series has exactly the coefficient pattern of Theorem IX: a = α = 1, b = m+k, β = m+n, and so on. The next page uses this to obtain continued fractions for such integrals, for example for the logarithm (asinh z).
errors: None on this page. The algebra of the continued-fraction derivation and the coefficient recursion checks out, including the signs and the identification B=(m+k)A/(m+n). (On the following page the last displayed partial denominator ends with '− etc.' where '+ etc.' is meant; that is trivial.)

ideas.what: Conversion of an alternating series with term ratios into a continued fraction whose convergents equal the partial sums
ideas.modern_name: Euler's continued fraction formula (equivalence of series and continued fractions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum (1748), ch. 18
ideas.where_published: Introductio I ch. 18; also E593 itself (Opuscula analytica II, 1785; Opera Omnia I.15)

ideas.what: Factoring Z = v(1+zⁿ)^{k/n} and solving the resulting first-order linear ODE by power series
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Pfaff transformation of ₂F₁, here as an instance yielding ₂F₁(1,b;c;w)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Inst. calc. int.; E710 etc.) and Pfaff (1797)
ideas.where_published: Institutiones calculi integralis; numerous Euler papers on integrals of the form ∫z^{m-1}(1+z^n)^{k/n-1}dz

ideas.what: Method of undetermined coefficients for series solution of a linear ODE with a z^m leading term

deep.surprise_reason: The page restates Euler's well-known series-to-continued-fraction equivalence and applies it to a standard binomial-integral (hypergeometric ₂F₁(1,b;c)) series found by undetermined coefficients. This is all classical Euler material, published in Opuscula analytica and in Opera Omnia I.15. The continued fraction does not accelerate convergence, and Gauss's 1813 continued fraction supersedes it.
transcription_corrections: No substantive corrections; the machine transcription matches the image. The table line '−z^{m−1} = −1' records the coefficient −1 placed under the z^{m−1} column, i.e. it pairs with mA.
